verdict.text: f3 is fixed.
The tutorial now says its commands ran with the kmctl release the page ships with.
That holds because `scripts/release.py set` re-pins the tutorial's install line to each release tag (it is in `DOC_FILES`).
The README hook snippet no longer pins `v0.3.0`, a tag that has no `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`.
It uses a `vX.Y.Z` placeholder, the same style the how-to pages use for `ref:`.
One small new issue: the comment on that line will go stale (f4).
It does not block.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: "stamp green: bec26f4a7de893e9e15039c12af80ddecef86f937f20547f492b50e52d137cc9".
Lint, tests and integration passed, and so did rows r1-r9 and r11-r13.
`docs/tutorials/get-started-with-kmctl.md` lines 1-30.
Line 14 now reads "with the kmctl release this page ships with".
The install line on line 22 is still `@v0.3.0`, and `release.py set` rewrites it through `_INSTALL`, so at each release the page names the release that was actually run.
`git diff main -- README.md`.
The `rev: vX.Y.Z` placeholder does not match `_INSTALL`, `_USES` or `_APM_PIN`, so `release.py set` leaves it alone and its `DOC_LINES` count of 6 is unchanged.
The release tests passed in the stamp.
`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` defines `kmctl-check`, the id the snippet uses.
f1: resolved in round 1.
The rule no longer says "lists every page".
f2: resolved in round 1.
f3: resolved at docs/tutorials/get-started-with-kmctl.md:14.
The line no longer names a version that predates `check --fix`.
f4: the README.md:209 comment "the hook ships from the next release" is true now, but becomes false once that release is out, and `release.py` will not touch it.
Something like "the hook needs kmctl 0.4.0 or later" (or whatever the first release with `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` will be) would stay true.
A plain fix is enough; it does not need to come back to me.
